PROPOSED INDICATOR AND THRESHOLD: Monitor the standard deviation of the excitation current over 1-minute intervals to detect contact instability. An increase in current variance indicates intermittent arcing and open-circuit transients caused by brush wear. The system fires an alarm when the 24-hour rolling standard deviation exceeds a calibrated threshold.
MECHANISM: As brush wear progresses, the contact interface degrades, causing intermittent electrical separation (micro-arcing) and increased contact resistance. This manifests as high-frequency current fluctuations that, even when sampled at 1-minute intervals, appear as increased statistical variance (RMS deviation) in the current magnitude rather than clean sinusoidal flow. This variance precedes thermal accumulation or mechanical vibration alarms.
DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: Standard practice relies on temperature rise or vibration analysis, which are lagging indicators of severe wear. This method uses the statistical stability of current magnitude as a leading indicator of contact integrity, detecting micro-arcing transients before macroscopic damage occurs.
LABELED PARAMETERS:
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Sampling interval = 1 minute (User Constraint)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Warning lead time = 2 weeks (User Constraint)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: False alarm limit = 1 per year per machine (User Constraint)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Contact voltage drop correlates with brush wear characteristics [doi:10.1109/holm.2018.8611774]
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Baseline standard deviation = 0.5% of rated current (your design choice; calibration based on healthy machine data)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Alarm threshold = 2.0% of rated current standard deviation (your design choice; 4x baseline to minimize false positives)
INDICATOR: Standard deviation of excitation current (A)
THRESHOLD: 2.0% of rated current (ASSUMPTION)
VALIDATION PROTOCOL: Test at rated temperature over a 4-week duration with n = 5 independent DEVICES (machines). Use a 1-week data window for calibration. Detection criterion: Standard deviation of excitation current > 2.0% of rated current.
